reviews.review: Would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys playing solo or with friends. The graphics are great and the soundtrack is even better. Sometimes a little buggy but nothing serious. I love the challenges aspect of the game, gives an interesting dynamic to the way that you play. The two things that make a game great is the soundtrack and way you play. Both hit that checkbox for me!

Awesome side-scrolling platformer with procedurally generated levels. Some people will attach the word "rogue" to this game because when you die, you're DEAD.

What's cool is the difficulty scales as you play the game. For me, the idea is that the longer you play, the better you get, the harder the game gets. I think it's pretty brilliant because this method allows you to play with increasing difficulty but it doesn't FEEL like the game is suddenly getting harder. You just sort of reach a point where you smash through a giant swath of crazy aliens and realize "Whoa, this is getting crazy" and look at the difficulty meter to see that it's in the "INSANE" section.

The gameplay is super fun. I will admit I died a TON at the start, but then I hooked up a gamepad and bound the keys to buttons that made sense for me and suddenly I felt like I had a grip of the game. If I had to use a keyboard I'd probably rebind the arrow keys to WASD and use the arrow keys for all four of the characters actions, making it almost like a hybrid twin-stick shooter. 

In each level you defeat enemies to gain money which eventually unlocks chests with power-ups that help you on your run. For example you may unlock a shield that will protect you during combat and regerenate when there are no enemies nearby, Once you defeat the level's boss and all the enemies in the level, you teleport to the next one where more craziness awaits. 

If you're a fan of platformers, I can't see anything you'd dislike about this game. The way the difficulty scales up WITH the player instead of AT the player is pretty awesome, and any game that can be difficult in a way that causes me to feel like "Ok I HAVE to do one more run" rather than "ok F*$% this game" gets a A+ from me.
